S4.name: Slugify CSV Dates CLI With Strict Mode

before.result:
I wrote `out/slugify-dates.py` and `out/README.md`, and ran a 4-row sample through the script in normal and strict modes. All four dates parse correctly, and the one bad date behaves as specified.

Sample input (the CSV is `title,date`, with the `Nov 22, 2026` field quoted):
```
"Launch Day: Café & Crème!",11/22/26
Hello World,2026-11-22
"Q4 Recap — Final","Nov 22, 2026"
Broken Date,2026-13-45
```

Normal mode (`python3 slugify-dates.py < sample.csv`), exit code 1:
```
slug,iso_date
launch-day-cafe-creme,2026-11-22
hello-world,2026-11-22
q4-recap-final,2026-11-22
error: bad date '2026-13-45' for title 'Broken Date'
broken-date,
```

Strict mode (`--strict`), exit code 2:
```
slug,iso_date
launch-day-cafe-creme,2026-11-22
hello-world,2026-11-22
q4-recap-final,2026-11-22
error: bad date '2026-13-45' for title 'Broken Date'
```

What I checked:
- Slugs are lowercase ASCII with hyphens; accents are stripped (Café → cafe) and punctuation collapses to single hyphens.
- All three date formats and the `11/22/26` short year produce `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- A bad date gives exit 2 in strict mode and stops at that row. In normal mode it prints an empty `iso_date`, writes a message to stderr, and exits 1.
- No network install was used.

- The spec didn't say what non-strict mode should do with a bad date, so I print an empty `iso_date` and exit 1. Tell me if you want a different behaviour.
